_comment: What counts as proof in this repository. Read by plugins/crucible/scripts/evidence_gate.py,
which reports these classes narrowed to a diff; it never decides whether the evidence exists.
This file is also dogfooding: without it hephaestus fell through to the implied class ('the
test suite passes'), which is exactly the default ADR-003 exists to move past. Two of the
classes below are things the suite genuinely cannot check, and one of them had already cost a
real failure before this file existed - see the ci-workflow class.

classes.when: Python under scripts/, plugins/**/scripts/, or evals/
classes.evidence: pytest green with no regression against the branch point (coverage_delta.py exit 0), and python_floor.py clean - a file that will not parse takes down collection for the whole suite, not just itself

classes.when: a SKILL.md, a command or an agent - prose that instructs a model
classes.evidence: skill_lint --strict clean, PLUS one of two branches - pick one and name it, the choice is the evidence. (a) PROSE THAT INSTRUCTS: the edit tells a model to do, refuse or prefer something, so the claim lives only in the prose and nothing else can falsify it. Requires a behavioral eval scenario in evals/scenarios.json asserting that claim. (b) PROSE THAT DESCRIBES: the edit documents behaviour implemented in scripts, so the prose is a mirror and the script is the thing. Requires naming the deterministic tests that pin the described behaviour, and at least one of them must fail if the description stops being true - a test that passes either way does not pin anything. Branch (b) is not the easy way out: it is harder to satisfy honestly, because naming the test forces you to check it exists. If NEITHER fits - the claim is real and nothing available can falsify it - say that out loud and record could-not-check. An untested instruction is not the same as a tested one, and the point of naming the branch is that 'it did not need a scenario' stops being something anyone can assert without argument

an actual run on a pull request, read from the job log. COULD-NOT-CHECK locally is the normal verdict here and must be recorded as such - this is not a formality: the python-floor matrix job added in ADR-003 passed every local check and failed on 3.9 the first time CI ran it, on an interpreter no local machine had

classes.when: release tooling, or anything that writes outside the repo
classes.evidence: a real invocation verified by the artefact it leaves behind - a tag, a file, an installed link - never by the command's return value
validate_manifests.py exit 0, and the plugin resolves under a real /plugin install
cms check clean, and check-public-safe.sh clean - the second is not optional in a public repo, and it has caught a real leak in an ADR
